title: Loom perception/decision contract
description: The single source of truth for the messages exchanged between the Loom body (Kotlin Paper plugin) and mind (Rust cognition service). The body sends a Perception; the mind returns a Decision. Union types use internal tagging: a discriminator property (Trigger.event, Intent.action) selects the variant and the variant's fields are inlined alongside it.

DecisionImportance.description: Importance tier that drives model routing on the mind side and is stamped onto every decision's provenance for the decision log.

Bearing.description: A horizontal compass bearing from the agent to something it can see. Four cardinal points and no finer, because it is the engine's own nearest-axis answer for the delta and a bearing precise enough to look like a heading would be a precision the body did not measure. here is the one value that is not a direction: the thing lies in the agent's own block column, within half a block horizontally - the block it stands on, a plant it stands in, something directly overhead - for which any compass point would be invented.

ObservationKind.description: What kind of world fact an observation describes. This is descriptive evidence, not policy: entity, block, and droppedItem are the three vanilla shapes the player body can offer back as request-scoped targets.

BlockFace.description: One face of a sensed support block. A place intent combines the support block's request-scoped ref with this face, so the location is chosen without accepting an arbitrary coordinate.

CoverFace.description: One of the nine faces around the two cells a standing body fills: the four cells beside its feet, the four beside its head, and the cell over its head. A creature can reach the body only through a face the server gives no collision.

Closing.description: One placement that would close an open face of the agent's cover: a held block placed against the named side of the named sensed support block lands in that face's cell.

block.description: The request-scoped ref of the sensed support block, in sight and in reach, to place against.

Cover.description: How enclosed the agent stands, read from the server's own ground at the cells around its body: what a shelter is made of. Server-observed geometry, never the mind's claim.

sealed.description: Whether the open space the body stands in is closed on every side: no cell of it, searched from the body's own two cells through every cell the server gives no collision, leads further than a small enclosure, so no creature can walk, climb or swim in. A sealed agent is sheltered.

walkOut.description: Whether a short walk leads out of where the body stands, by the steps a body makes. False in a pit deeper than a jump or a sealed shelter: no flight can run from there.

open.description: The faces around the body the server gives no collision, each at most once.

closings.description: For open faces a held block could close from where the body stands, one placement each, at most one per face.

descend.description: The ref of the block under the body's feet when digging it drops the body onto solid ground into a cell more enclosed than this one, with no water let in: the one dig that deepens a shelter. Absent otherwise.

blockItems.description: Items something in sight can give the agent now - a dig in reach or a drop in sight - that place as a solid block: what a shelter can be closed with when nothing held can.

gathers.description: For a shelter whose faces can close but nothing held can close them: the refs of blocks in reach a safe dig of which yields a solid block - none of the shelter's own faces, its roof or its floor - and of solid dropped items in sight, whose gathering is a step of the shelter goal itself rather than a goal of its own. Absent when there is nothing to gather or nothing to close.

CoverProgress.description: A shelter goal's body-measured cover: how many of the nine faces around the body are closed, how many more a held block could close from where it stands, and whether the space it stands in is sealed.

EquipmentDestination.description: The equipment destination the mind chose for one offered inventory stack. These are Mineflayer's bounded player equipment destinations, translated at the body-control boundary rather than guessed from a slot number.

EntityRef.description: A short opaque handle for one world target the body observed: a living entity, a nearby block, or a dropped item. It is valid only inside the single perception that issued it and only for the agent that perception belongs to. It carries no meaning the mind may parse: it is not a name, type, coordinate, entity id, or slot, and two things that are alike in every other way still get different refs. The intent variant determines which target store may resolve it, so a block ref used as an item ref is refused rather than reinterpreted.

SlotRef.description: A short opaque handle for one stack in the body's own inventory, valid only inside the single perception that issued it and only for the agent that perception belongs to. It is the same shape of handle as an EntityRef and named separately because it means something different: it resolves to one slot of the body's own container rather than to a thing in the world, and the stack standing in that slot may have changed by the time a decision arrives, so the body re-reads the slot and refuses what it finds there if it is no longer food. It carries no meaning the mind may parse, and a ref from any other request or any other agent is refused rather than resolved.

RecipeRef.description: A short opaque handle for one exact currently craftable recipe offered by the body. It is valid only inside the single perception that issued it and only for that agent. It is not a recipe id or item name, and the body retains the exact Mineflayer recipe, current ingredient snapshot, and any required workstation behind it.

InventoryStack.description: One occupied slot of the body's own inventory, as the body describes it. It is the whole of what the mind is told about what it is carrying, and it carries a handle so a decision can name one exact stack back rather than a kind of item.

ref.description: The handle by which a decision may name this exact stack back to the body.

what.description: What the stack holds, as the body describes it. A description for the mind to reason with, never the handle: two slots can hold the same item and be different stacks.

count.description: How many items the stack holds. At least one, because an empty slot is not reported at all.

edible.description: Whether the server says the stack can be eaten. Absent when the body did not say, which reads as no: a meal is offered only from a stack the server named food.

solid.description: Whether the server says the stack places as a solid block, one no creature passes. Absent when the body did not say, which reads as no: a shelter is closed only with a stack the server named solid.

held.description: Whether the server says the stack is in the main hand, which a placement must already be holding. Absent when the body did not say, which reads as no.

CraftingOption.description: One exact recipe the body found craftable from the current inventory and, when required, one retained reachable crafting table. The ref is the only value a craft intent may name back; the descriptive result and bounds let the mind choose without learning a registry id.

ref.description: The request-scoped handle for this exact recipe and retained workstation choice.

what.description: The result item, as the body describes it.

resultCount.description: How many result items one application of this recipe produces.

maxCrafts.description: The most recipe applications the current ingredients and Loom's per-request item bound permit. A craft intent chooses a positive count no larger than this value.

requiresTable.description: Whether the retained exact recipe requires the reachable crafting table held behind this offer.

DayPhase.description: Which part of the world's day it is. Derived from the level's own day time, so an agent can tell midday from dusk without being told the raw tick count.

WorldState.description: The bounded world clock the body reveals. Survival depends on it - what is safe at midday is not safe at night - and it is a fact about the world rather than about the body, which is why it is named separately from the rest of the self-state it rides in.

isDay.description: Whether it is daylight where the body stands, as the level itself answers it. Distinct from dayPhase because a dimension with a fixed time has a day time and no daylight.

ticksUntilNightfall.description: Ticks from now until the next nightfall, wrapping the world's day. Always positive: during the night it counts to the following nightfall, and dayPhase is what says the night is already here.

SelfState.description: The bounded self-state the body chose to reveal. Owned primitives only, so the mind cannot reach back into world state through it.

health.description: Current health of the agent's body.

food.description: The player's vanilla food level, kept separate from health and saturation. Zero is starvation pressure, not evidence of death; only the server witness establishes death.

saturation.description: The player's vanilla saturation reserve, spent before food falls. It is reported separately because a full food bar with no saturation and one with a full reserve are different survival states.

position.description: World position [x, y, z]. Continuous coordinates.

inventorySummary.description: The player's complete inventory window, one entry per occupied slot and nothing for an empty one, bounded by its 46 addressable slots. Each entry carries the handle by which an eat may name that exact stack, so what the mind may act on is exactly what it was told it is carrying.

craftingOptions.description: The exact currently craftable recipes this bounded perception offers. Each option is request-scoped and retains its ingredient snapshot and any required crafting table inside the body.

craftingOptionsOmitted.description: How many otherwise craftable recipe offers the body omitted because the bounded list was full. Required and never negative, so an empty or short list cannot be mistaken for a complete recipe catalogue.

ownDrops.description: What the server saw this agent's own recent digs drop, newest first, attributed to the request whose dig dropped it. Told to the digger whether or not the drop is in sight, and whatever became of it since, so a dig that dropped something another agent then took is still known to have yielded.

cover.description: How enclosed the agent stands, from the server's ground. Absent where the body has no server ground to read.

GoalRefusal.description: One goal decision the body refused before acting: which request, the countable outcome tag it was refused with, and - for a success condition it judged - the item, the total asked for, how many were held and how many more what was in sight could give.

OwnDrop.description: One stack the server dropped for one of this agent's digs. fate is what became of it: lying where the server can still see it, collected by this agent, taken by another player, or gone (merged, despawned or destroyed). distance, direction and verticalOffset place a lying drop from the agent now, measured the way an observation's are, and are present exactly when fate is lying.

requestId.description: The perception request id of the decision whose dig dropped this stack.

ref.description: The dropped-item observation in this perception that is this drop, so a collect may name it; present only for a lying drop the body offered, in sight or not.

DropFate.description: What became of a stack an agent's own dig dropped.

BlockYield.description: One item digging a block with what the body holds can drop, and how many: the server's loot rules are random, so least is the fewest it dropped in the server's sampled rolls and most the most, a least of 0 means a dig may drop none of it at all, and perHundred is how many of it a hundred digs drop on average in those rolls - the expected yield, which for a rare drop is far below the middle of its range. perHundred lies between 100 times least and 100 times most.

Observation.description: One already-summarized observation the body chose to reveal. The perception carries a list of these instead of a live world handle.

what.description: Human-readable summary of the observed thing.

distance.description: Distance from the agent to the observed thing, in blocks.

verticalOffset.description: How far above the agent the observed thing is, in blocks; negative if it is below. Separate from the bearing because a bearing is horizontal and a thing on a cliff is not reachable by walking toward it.

visible.description: Whether the body has an unobstructed line of sight to the observed thing. False means the body knows it is there and cannot see it - through a wall, or round a corner - which is a different situation from not knowing at all.

ref.description: The request-scoped handle by which a decision may name this particular entity, block, or dropped item back to the body. Every player-body world observation is actionable as exactly the kind it states, and a mind must name this handle rather than inventing a coordinate, entity id, item name, or slot.

count.description: How many items the dropped-item entity currently represents. Present only when kind is droppedItem; absent for entities and blocks. The bindings enforce that relation.

routeRefused.description: Present, and true, only for a dropped item this agent's body has already found no way to from where it stands: no route at all, for as long as the item lives (r15), or a route its approach stalled on from this same cell to the item's, over the same ground (r34 delta). It is not offered to collect and gives nothing a goal may count on.

hunts.description: Present, and true, only for a creature that hunts the agent's kind, by the body's own list of player hunters: what a goal review may flee from (r20: kappa reviewed at health 7.7 beside a zombie and a skeleton, was offered only dirt digs, and died).

yields.description: The items digging this block with what the body holds can drop, each with the range the server's own random loot rules give: empty when it drops nothing, such as bare-hand terracotta. Never air. Present only when kind is block.

digSafe.description: Whether digging this block is safe: it leaves the body a way out, its drop where the body can collect it, the body dry, and, at night or as nightfall nears, the sealed space the body stands in sealed. Present only when kind is block.

standable.description: Whether a body can stand at this block: on top of a solid block with two open cells above it, or in the own cell of a block the server gives no collision, with solid ground below and an open cell above. Read from the server's ground rather than from sight, because a block whose face is visible can still be covered. Present only when kind is block; absent for entities and dropped items. The bindings enforce that relation.

cover.description: For a block a body can stand at, how many of the nine faces around the cell it would stand in the server gives collision: natural cover in sight, nine for a cell closed on every side. Present only for a standable block.

Trigger.description: The event that triggered cognition. There is intentionally no per-tick variant: cognition is event-driven, never per-tick. Internally tagged on the 'event' property.

oneOf.title: Spoken
oneOf.description: Another actor spoke to or near the agent.

oneOf.title: Damaged
oneOf.description: The agent's body took damage.

attackerRef.description: The creature that dealt the damage - a projectile's shooter, not the projectile - as the ref this perception's own surroundings name it by, so a flight or a strike can name the one creature that hurt the agent rather than the nearest of its kind. Present only when the server identified the attacker and this perception shows it; such an attacker is always among the surroundings and always offered to flee and to attack within reach, however many nearer creatures there are. Absent for damage no creature dealt, and for an attacker the body could not see or report.

healthBefore.description: The server's own health of the agent's body when the hit landed, before it was applied. Present together with healthAfter whenever the server witnessed the hit.

healthAfter.description: The server's own health of the agent's body once the hit was applied: its health before the hit less the hit's final damage, never below zero. A damaged perception's selfState.health is this value, because the body's own reading can still be the one before the hit (r34: alpha took 14 from a creeper and was shown health 20 when it had 6 left). Present together with healthBefore.

oneOf.title: ThreatSighted
oneOf.description: A living thing that hunts this agent's kind came into the body's view. Everything the body already verified about it travels with the trigger, so the mind never has to ask a second question to decide whether to run: which thing it is (as a ref it can name back), how far and in which direction it lies, whether the body can actually see it, and whether the engine's own bounded ground search found a route to it.

threat.description: What the thing is, as the body describes it. A description for the mind to reason with, never the handle: naming a threat by what it is would leave the body guessing which of two identical creatures was meant.

distance.description: Distance from the agent to the threat, in blocks, measured the same way an observation's distance is.

visible.description: Whether the body has an unobstructed line of sight to the threat. False is not safety: it means the body knows the threat is there and something stands between them.

reachable.description: Whether the engine's own bounded ground search found a route that reaches the threat. It is the search the body made from itself toward the threat, not the threat's toward the body, so false means no walkable route was found within the body's own budgeted search - a fenced-off or cliff-separated threat, and not a promise that nothing is coming. It is the result of a search the body already paid for, not an invitation for the mind to ask for another. Absent when the body made no such search, which is the player body's case: it was a constant false there, and the mind read it as no route to flee (r20).

oneOf.title: BlockSighted
oneOf.description: A notable block came into the agent's view.

oneOf.title: PlanReview
oneOf.description: A planning call: the agent's objective, subgoals and current steps are set. cause is start, subgoalDone, blocked or checkIn; reason is the step model's stated reason for asking.

oneOf.title: GoalReview
oneOf.description: A scheduled prompt for the agent to reconsider its goals. Empty variant.

oneOf.title: StepSettled
oneOf.description: The step the agent's held goal last took has ended, so the agent reviews that goal again at once rather than at its next scheduled review. At most one follows each scheduled goal review. Empty variant.

Perception.description: The bounded snapshot the body exposes to the mind. Carries no world handle: this is the entire surface the mind sees.

requestId.description: Correlates this perception with the decision the mind returns.

agentId.description: Stable identifier of the agent whose body produced this perception.

capturedTick.description: The server tick on which the body captured this snapshot.

surroundings.description: The summarized observations the body chose to reveal, bounded to 48 entities, 48 blocks, and 48 dropped items before they are combined into this one deterministic list.

surroundingsOmitted.description: How many otherwise eligible observations the body's own count bound dropped before this perception was serialized: things that were in range, alive and would have been described, and are not in surroundings. Required and never negative, so a mind cannot read the absence of the field as a complete view of the scene. Zero is the ordinary case and says the list is everything the body had. Out-of-range and ineligible things are not omissions - they were never observations.

goal.description: The agent's held short-term goal, present only on a goalReview or stepSettled perception and only while one is held.

lastRefusal.description: Why the body refused the agent's previous goal decision before acting on it, told once, at the next goalReview or stepSettled perception.

explore.description: Cells beyond what the body can see where it can stand, one per compass bearing at most, each a moveTo target named by its ref, so an agent that sees nothing worth doing can walk to look further. They state no more than where a body can stand; what lies there is unknown until the body senses it.

recalled.description: Sources of items the body saw recently and does not see now, nearest first: where the nearest one of each item was, and the expected yield of a dig of it in hundredths. A goal for a recalled item is walked toward by the cells at the edge of sight in its direction (r20: no agent without a log in sight could set a log goal, and the only walk to the edge of sight came with an abandon).

horizon.description: Goal items the agent may set a total for beyond what sight alone guarantees, each grounded in a source seen now or remembered, or in a known recipe whose input is so grounded, with the most a goal of it may ask: past what the grounding gives only onto ground beyond the edge of sight. Nothing the agent's own footing guarantees grounds one (r22: every goal was dirt from underfoot, and no agent looked for wood).

plan.description: The agent's own plan, kept by the body from its earlier answers.

recent.description: The agent's latest actions, oldest first, with what the body answered and how its inventory changed after each.

Plan.description: A model-owned plan in three levels: a long-term objective, its ordered subgoals, and the ordered steps of the current subgoal. Subgoals before 'subgoal' and steps before 'step' are done; 'step' equal to the number of steps means the current subgoal's steps are all done, and 'subgoal' equal to the number of subgoals means the objective's subgoals are all done.

RecentAction.description: One past action of the agent: the intent's action tag, the body's outcome tag, and the inventory change seen at the next perception.

ItemChange.description: How many of one item the inventory gained (positive) or lost (negative).

PlanUpdate.description: What a decision does to the agent's plan. Internally tagged on the 'update' property. Step calls continue, mark a step done or ask for a replan; only a planning call sets the objective and subgoals.

oneOf.title: Continue
oneOf.description: Step model: keep the plan; this decision works on the current step.

oneOf.title: StepDone
oneOf.description: Step model: the current step is done; this decision starts the next.

oneOf.title: Replan
oneOf.description: Step model: the current subgoal is blocked; ask the planner for a new plan, for the reason given.

oneOf.title: ReplacePlan
oneOf.description: Planner only: the objective, the ordered remaining subgoals (the first is current) and its steps, for the reason given.

RecalledSource.description: Where the body last saw a source of an item it does not see now, placed from the agent the way an observation is.

HorizonGoal.description: One goal item the agent may set a total for beyond what sight guarantees, what grounds it, and the most a goal of it may ask.

grounding.description: What grounds the goal: a source in sight now, a source remembered out of sight, or a known recipe whose input `via` is grounded by either.

via.description: For a recipe-grounded goal, the grounded input its recipe is made from; absent otherwise.

most.description: The largest total a goal of this item may ask, counting what is held.

frontier.description: Whether that total reaches past what the grounding gives, onto ground beyond the edge of sight.

ExploreTarget.description: One standable cell at the edge of sight, placed from the agent the way an observation is.

Intent.description: A named intent the mind returns. The body validates and applies it; the mind never mutates world state directly. Internally tagged on the 'action' property.

oneOf.title: Say
oneOf.description: Speak a line of text.

oneOf.title: MoveTo
oneOf.description: Walk to stand on top of one nearby block named by the request-scoped ref it carried in the perception being answered. A ref rather than coordinates on purpose: a perception states where things are as a bearing, a distance and a vertical offset, never as coordinates, so a coordinate the mind wrote was a guess - and in a live run every such guess that failed named open air. The body resolves the ref against that one request only and walks to where a body stands on the exact sensed block: the cell directly above a solid block, or the block's own cell where the server gives it no collision (a dead bush, grass, a flower). The ground decides whether that cell can be reached and stood in, and nothing below the mind picks another one.

oneOf.title: Walk
oneOf.description: Walk blocks blocks along the compass bearing of one cell at the edge of sight (an explore ref from the perception being answered), in consecutive bounded hops. No cap but the world border: the walk stops only on arrival, a stall (a hop that makes no headway), or danger (a newer decision takes the body).

oneOf.title: Flee
oneOf.description: Move away from one living thing, named by the ref it carried in the perception being answered. A ref rather than a name or a type on purpose: two identical creatures are different threats, and the body must retreat from the one the mind meant. The body resolves the ref against that one request only, and refuses a ref it did not issue for that request rather than guessing.

oneOf.title: Eat
oneOf.description: Eat one item from one stack of the body's own inventory, named by the ref that stack carried in the perception being answered. A ref rather than an item name on purpose: two slots can hold the same item, and the body must consume the one the mind meant. The body resolves the ref against that one request only, re-reads the slot it names, and refuses what it finds there if it is no longer food - so a stack that changed between the perception and the decision is refused rather than substituted. On acceptance Mineflayer asks vanilla to consume exactly one item; the next perception reports the resulting food and saturation separately.

oneOf.title: Dig
oneOf.description: Dig one nearby block named by the request-scoped ref in the perception being answered. The body re-reads the exact block immediately before asking Mineflayer to dig it, uses only the item already held, and refuses a removed, changed, hidden, unreachable, or undiggable target.

oneOf.title: DigSequence
oneOf.description: Dig nearby blocks, each named by a request-scoped ref in the perception being answered, in order. Each step is one Dig through the same checks; the sequence stops at the first step that does not dig its block.

oneOf.title: Collect
oneOf.description: Collect one nearby dropped-item entity named by the request-scoped ref in the perception being answered. approach explicitly permits one bounded path to the position that exact item occupied when the request was admitted; false permits no movement.

oneOf.title: Place
oneOf.description: Place one offered inventory stack that is already held against one face of one nearby sensed support block. Both refs come from the perception being answered; the body revalidates the held stack, the support block, the destination, visibility, and reach before asking Mineflayer to place exactly once.

oneOf.title: Equip
oneOf.description: Equip one inventory stack offered by the perception being answered into the destination the mind chose. The body re-reads the exact slot immediately before invoking Mineflayer and reports the actual destination slot Mineflayer used.

oneOf.title: Craft
oneOf.description: Apply one exact recipe offered by this perception a bounded number of times. The body revalidates the recipe, complete inventory snapshot, output bound, and retained crafting table immediately before invoking Mineflayer. It gathers nothing and chooses no substitute recipe.

oneOf.title: Attack
oneOf.description: Attack one exact living entity with one exact offered inventory stack for at most the chosen bounded strike count. approach explicitly permits one bounded path to the target's admitted position; false permits no movement. The body never changes targets or starts an open-ended pursuit.

oneOf.title: Sleep
oneOf.description: Try to sleep in one exact bed offered by this perception, retaining ownership only until vanilla wakes the player or Loom's bounded wait ends. The body selects no other bed and never decides whether the server should skip the night.

oneOf.title: Rest
oneOf.description: Stop, and hold this position on purpose. It restores nothing: hunger continues under vanilla's own food and saturation rules while a resting agent waits. It is its own intent rather than a synonym for idle because deliberately waiting somewhere - sealed in for the night, say - is a choice a run must be able to count separately from having decided nothing. Empty variant.

oneOf.title: Idle
oneOf.description: Do nothing this cycle. Empty variant.

GoalStatement.description: One short-term goal in the agent's own words. Bounded so a carried goal can never grow a perception: it is the whole of what one review hands the next.

IntentAction.description: The action an Intent takes, as its action tag. A held goal's typed step is the action its affirming decision's intent took.

ItemName.description: An item exactly as the body names it in an inventory stack's what, such as item.minecraft.stick: always item.namespace.path. A success condition names the item its goal must hold.

GoalDisposition.description: What a goal review's decision does with the agent's short-term goal. adopt starts one where none is held; continue keeps the held goal; revise changes the held goal's target under the same goalId; replace abandons the held goal and adopts a new one in the same answer, under this decision's own id; complete and abandon end it. adopt, continue, revise and replace take the decision's intent as the goal's step, so the body refuses them beside an idle or rest intent, which is no step.

GoalStepResult.description: The mind's verdict on the step its previous goal review took, judged against the progress evidence the carried goal states: done finished that step, progressing moved it forward, noProgress did not.

GoalReason.description: Why a replace or an abandon ends the held goal, by evidence the body checks: completed, its success condition is met (a replace only); impossible, what is held and could be given no longer reaches it, or no shelter step exists; stale, it advanced nothing for the stall bound's steps in a row; unsafe, a shelter goal replaces another as night nears and the agent stands exposed; superseded, a replace by a different objective, chosen deliberately for the reason the decision's reasoning states.

GoalChoice.description: A decision's explicit, machine-auditable choice about the agent's short-term goal. successItem and successCount are the goal and its success condition: holding that many of that item in total, counting what is held now, which the body measures and words itself. Both are for adopt, revise and replace, and the body refuses a count fewer than two beyond what the inventory holds plus the agent's own drops of the item lying in reach - a goal one step could meet is no objective - or one more than it holds plus what is in sight could give, and applies the upper bound to a continue; more of the held goal's own item is a revise, which keeps the goal, never a replace. step words the one concrete next step this decision's intent takes toward the goal, for adopt, continue, revise and replace; the body types that step from the intent itself, and refuses one that cannot produce the goal's item. stepResult judges the carried goal's previous step, for every disposition except adopt. The body refuses a choice missing a field its disposition requires, and ignores the rest. reason states why a replace or an abandon ends the held goal, and the body refuses either without one, or with one its evidence does not support.

discover.description: For an adopt or replace with no success item: a discovery goal, whose success condition is that a walk to the edge of sight reveals a useful resource no footing gives, set only while no item goal is grounded, stepped only by such a walk, and replaced by an item goal once it reveals one (r23: 17 of 70 reviews could set no goal at all).

shelter.description: For an adopt or replace with no success item: a shelter goal, whose success condition is that the server's ground seals the space the agent stands in, stepped by a dig that deepens the cover, a placement that closes an open face, or a walk onto natural cover, and offered as night nears or while it lasts.

feeds.description: For an adopt while a shelter goal is held and nothing held can close it: the item goal adopted is a resource subgoal that feeds the shelter goal, which waits under it and is held again once the subgoal is completed or abandoned. Historical: from routine-v36 gathering a closer is a step of the shelter goal itself, and no subgoal is offered.

GoalProgress.description: Body-measured evidence about the goal since its last affirming review, never claimed by the mind. conditionHeld is how many of the success item the inventory holds now and conditionMet whether that reaches successCount. inventoryDelta is every item whose held count changed. conditionAdvanced says the held count rose; stepAdvanced says the typed step was carried out, which for a walk means arriving somewhere the goal had not been. stepsWithoutProgress counts affirmed steps in a row that advanced neither; moving about, falling or returning advances nothing.

cover.description: For a shelter goal, its cover as this review measured it; conditionMet then says the cover is sealed.

StepEvidence.description: What showed the goal's last step was carried out: arrived for a walk that reached its visible target somewhere new to the goal, gained for an action after which the inventory held more of the goal's item, gainedInput for one after which it held more of a direct input of a recipe for the goal's item, dropped for a dig the server saw drop something for this agent's own request, wherever it went after, revealed for a walk to the edge of sight that arrived where a source of the goal's item was then in sight, covered for a shelter goal's step after which the server's ground showed the agent more enclosed than the goal had yet been - more faces closed, or more closable from where it stands, or sealed - none when nothing did. Only a step with evidence advances.

InventoryChange.description: How the held count of one item changed since the goal's last affirming review: positive gained, negative lost, never zero.

GoalStep.description: The last step taken under a held goal: the decision that most recently adopted, continued, or revised it, the intent it chose, and the body's own outcome tag for that intent.

requestId.description: The request id of that decision, so the step joins to its decided and intentApplied records.

outcome.description: The body's countable outcome tag for that intent, the same tag its intentApplied record carries.

GoalSummary.description: The one short-term goal the agent's previous goal review left held, carried into a goalReview or stepSettled perception and no other trigger. Body-owned state, isolated per agent and bounded in size and lifetime.

goalId.description: Stable for the goal's whole life: the request id of the decision that adopted it.

revision.description: How many times the goal has been revised since it was adopted.

adoptedTick.description: The server tick on which the goal was adopted.

step.description: The step the goal's last affirming review chose to take.

stepAction.description: The action the step's decision's intent took.

stepRef.description: The ref that intent acted on, absent for an action that names none.

discovery.description: Whether the goal is a discovery goal: no success item, met when a walk to the edge of sight reveals a useful resource no footing gives.

shelter.description: Whether the goal is a shelter goal: no success item, met when the server's ground seals the space the agent stands in.

feeds.description: For a resource subgoal, the goalId of the shelter goal it feeds, which is held again once this goal is completed or abandoned.

Provenance.description: Reproducibility stamp attached to every decision and written to the append-only decision log, so each decision's perception -> reasoning -> action -> result chain can be replayed and audited.

model.description: Identifier of the model that produced the decision.

promptVersion.description: Version of the prompt template used, for reproducibility.

Decision.description: The structured decision the mind returns for a Perception.

requestId.description: Echoes the Perception.requestId this decision answers.

agentId.description: Echoes the Perception.agentId this decision is for.

reasoning.description: The mind's natural-language justification, logged for research.

goal.description: The decision's explicit choice about the agent's short-term goal. Absent means no choice, which leaves any held goal unchanged.

plan.description: What this decision does to the agent's plan. Absent is a continue.
